268: The sun was now resting upon the crest of the western hills of Emmaus, hanging low on the horizon and painting the sky in deep amber, crimson, and violet hues. A fresh evening breeze began to stir from the mountain passes. The fine chalk dust of the road, kicked up by their sandals, hung suspended in the golden evening light.
269: Jesus was now approaching the climax of his discourse, having illuminated the hidden treasures of the Pentateuch and the Sacred Poetry. Yet there remained the burning visions of the Prophets.
270: Though radiating unshakeable peace, his voice now carried a solemn, compelling urgency.
271: The gaze of the two disciples was torn between the fading splendor of the twilight road and the overwhelming presence of this mysterious traveler. Their faces, once sunken in grief and confusion, now shone with breathless wonder and reverent fascination. It was hard to tell whether they were breathless from the steep ascent or from the fire blazing within their souls.
272: Nathaniel leaned over and whispered into Cleopas's ear:
273: "Cleopas... who is this man? He no longer seems a stranger to me. He does not speak like the pilgrims who journey through Judea, nor like the scribes of Jerusalem. When he explains the Scriptures, he does not merely recall dead words—he speaks as though he stood present at the very hour when those eternal covenants were ratified! Do you not feel the very same fire burning in your chest as he walks with us?"
277: "Listen now to Isaiah, the prince of the prophets. When King Ahaz trembled in fear before the allied armies of Syria and Ephraim, the Lord offered him a miraculous sign—any sign, whether in the deepest depths or the highest heavens. Ahaz, in false piety, refused. Then Isaiah declared, centuries before the Messiah's birth:
278: *"Therefore the Lord himself will give you a sign: The virgin will conceive and give birth to a son, and will call him Immanuel."* [Is 7:14]
279: "A Son born of a virgin! And his name would be Immanuel—meaning *'God with us'*. God would not remain distant in the heavenly heights: he would come down to dwell with us in person, clothed in human flesh."[EN_REF:41]
280: **25. Isaiah - The Child Who Reigns - Prince of Peace (Isaiah 9:6-7)**
282: "And Isaiah saw even further. He beheld that this Son would be no ordinary ruler:
283: *"For to us a child is born, to us a son is given, and the government will be on his shoulders. And he will be called Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace. Of the greatness of his government and peace there will be no end. He will reign on David's throne and over his kingdom, establishing and upholding it with justice and righteousness from that time on and forever."* [Is 9:6-7]
284: "Look closely at the divine titles Isaiah gives this child: Mighty God! Everlasting Father! This child born of woman is at once true man and bearer of the majesty of Almighty God. He shall sit upon David's throne—fulfilling the eternal covenant spoken through Nathan. And of his reign and of his peace there will never be an end."[EN_REF:42]
287: "And Isaiah saw the Messiah spring forth—not from a proud cedar, but from a felled stump:
288: *"A shoot will come up from the stump of Jesse; from his roots a Branch will bear fruit. The Spirit of the LORD will rest on him— the Spirit of wisdom and of understanding, the Spirit of counsel and of might, the Spirit of the knowledge and fear of the LORD."* [Is 11:1-2]
289: "The stump of Jesse—the royal line of David—would be cut down. The earthly monarchy would fall into ruin. Yet from its roots, from an apparently lifeless stump, a living Branch would blossom. The sevenfold fullness of the Spirit of the Lord would rest upon him, spreading the knowledge of God across the world:
290: *"For the earth will be filled with the knowledge of the LORD as the waters cover the sea."* [Is 11:9]
291: "And he would rule in righteousness, establishing the Kingdom of Heaven that—believe me—has already begun in power, experienced by you even now until its glorious consummation, when every creature under heaven acknowledges that Jesus reigns and shall return in glory.
294: "Now we arrive at that which has proven hardest for your hearts to embrace, yet which is the most vital of all. Isaiah spoke of a Servant of the Lord—a Servant who would accomplish a redemptive work that no king, priest, or prophet before him could ever achieve.
295: "In the First Song, the Servant is presented:
296: *"Here is my servant, whom I uphold, my chosen one in whom I delight; I will put my Spirit on him, and he will bring justice to the nations. He will not shout or cry out, or raise his voice in the streets. A bruised reed he will not break, and a smoldering wick he will not snuff out. In faithfulness he will bring forth justice."* [Is 42:1-3]
297: "In the Second Song, the Servant is consecrated from his mother's womb:
298: *"Before I was born the LORD called me; from my mother's womb he has spoken my name... 'It is too small a thing for you to be my servant to restore the tribes of Jacob... I will also make you a light for the Gentiles, that my salvation may reach to the ends of the earth.'"* [Is 49:1, 6]
299: "In the Third Song, the Servant willingly yields his body to shame:
300: *"I offered my back to those who beat me, my cheeks to those who pulled out my beard; I did not hide my face from mocking and spitting."* [Is 50:6]
301: "And in the Fourth Song, the Servant suffers, atones, and dies for our sins.
302: "Listen now with quiet reverence. These are the sacred words that explain everything that has transpired in Jerusalem these past days:
303: *"See, my servant will act wisely; he will be raised and lifted up and highly exalted."* [Is 52:13]
304: *"He was despised and rejected by mankind, a man of suffering, and familiar with pain... and we held him in low esteem."* [Is 53:3]
305: *"Surely he took up our pain and bore our suffering, yet we considered him punished by God, stricken by him, and afflicted."* [Is 53:4]
306: *"But he was pierced for our transgressions, he was crushed for our iniquities; the punishment that brought us peace was on him, and by his wounds we are healed."* [Is 53:5]
307: *"We all, like sheep, have gone astray, each of us has turned to our own way; and the LORD has laid on him the iniquity of us all."* [Is 53:6]
308: *"He was oppressed and afflicted, yet he did not open his mouth; he was led like a lamb to the slaughter, and as a sheep before its shearers is silent, so he did not open his mouth."* [Is 53:7]
309: *"He was assigned a grave with the wicked, and with the rich in his death, though he had done no violence, nor was any deceit in his mouth."* [Is 53:9]
310: *"Yet it was the LORD's will to crush him and cause him to suffer, and though the LORD makes his life an offering for sin, he will see his offspring and prolong his days, and the will of the LORD will prosper in his hand."* [Is 53:10]
311: *"After he has suffered, he will see the light of life and be satisfied; by his knowledge my righteous servant will justify many, and he will bear their iniquities."* [Is 53:11]
312: "Friends, do you hear the voice of Isaiah? His prophecy affirms that the Messiah, the Righteous One, was wounded for our transgressions. I repeat: for our transgressions—not his own! The Lord laid upon him the iniquity of us all. There was no deceit found in his mouth, yet it pleased the Father to crush him, rendering his life an offering for sin. He was the ultimate sacrifice: the true Passover Lamb, the scapegoat of the Day of Atonement, the guilt offering—not an animal, but a Man: the Servant of the Lord.
313: "It was necessary that the Messiah should suffer these things—not by tragic misfortune, not in defeat, but according to the eternal purpose of God. The death of the Messiah is the propitiation for the sins of the world! And behold: Isaiah declares that *'he will see his offspring'* and *'prolong his days'*. After laying down his life as an offering for sin... can a man behold his offspring after death, unless... he rises again from the dead?"[EN_REF:43]
314: **28. Isaiah - Anointed to Proclaim Good News (Isaiah 61:1-3)**
316: "And Isaiah foretold the public ministry of the Servant:
317: *"The Spirit of the Sovereign LORD is on me, because the LORD has anointed me to proclaim good news to the poor. He has sent me to bind up the brokenhearted, to proclaim freedom for the captives and release from darkness for the prisoners, to proclaim the year of the LORD's favor and the day of vengeance of our God, to comfort all who mourn."* [Is 61:1-2]
318: "The Messiah was not to come merely as a political conqueror. He was to come first as a preacher of good tidings, a healer of the brokenhearted, a deliverer—not primarily from Roman or Greek legions, but from the eternal tyranny of sin and death."
319: Cleopas halted in the middle of the road, wiping the dust and sweat from his forehead with the sleeve of his cloak, and looked upon their Traveling Companion with eyes filled with tears. The sharp edge of grief had yielded to an unutterable peace. With a voice shaking with emotion, he gently interrupted him:
320: "How can this be? As you speak, the crushing ache in our hearts simply vanishes away. It is as if every passage of the Law and the Prophets, which once seemed hidden behind a heavy veil of shadows, has suddenly burst into living light pointing to a single face!"
321: **29. Jeremiah - The Righteous Branch and the New Covenant (Jeremiah 23:5-6; 31:31-34)**
323: "Yes, Cleopas!" said Jesus with infinite tenderness. "The Word of God comforts and transforms the human heart."
324: And he continued concerning the prophets of the Lord:
325: "And what of Jeremiah, who witnessed the destruction of Jerusalem? Did he not prophesy that out of the house of David the Lord would raise up a King who would reign wisely and execute justice? Hear what is written:
326: *"'The days are coming,' declares the LORD, 'when I will raise up for David a righteous Branch, a King who will reign wisely and do what is just and right in the land. In his days Judah will be saved and Israel will live in safety. This is the name by which he will be called: The LORD Our Righteous Savior.'"* [Jr 23:5-6]
327: "The name of the Branch is *'The LORD Our Righteousness'*—Yahweh Tsidkenu! The Messiah bears the very name of the living God!
328: "And Jeremiah prophesied something even more magnificent—a new covenant:
329: *"'The days are coming,' declares the LORD, 'when I will make a new covenant with the people of Israel and with the people of Judah... I will put my law in their minds and write it on their hearts. I will be their God, and they will be my people... For I will forgive their wickedness and will remember their sins no more.'"* [Jr 31:31, 33-34]
330: "A new covenant! Inscribed not on tablets of stone, but upon the living tablets of the heart. And the foundation of this covenant, understand, is the full and everlasting forgiveness of sins."
333: "Ezekiel, in exile by the Kebar River, heard the Lord promise a Shepherd:
334: *"I will place over them one shepherd, my servant David, and he will tend them; he will tend them and be their shepherd. I the LORD will be their God, and my servant David will be prince among them."* [Ez 34:23-24]
335: *"'My servant David will be king over them, and they will all have one shepherd.'"* [Ez 37:24]
336: "God called this prince *'My servant David'*. But how could that be, when King David had been dead for centuries? The meaning is unmistakably clear: Ezekiel speaks of David's royal Descendant—the Messiah—who is the true Shepherd of Israel, tending his flock in righteousness and peace."
337: **31. Daniel - The Son of Man and the Seventy Weeks (Daniel 7:13-14; 9:24-27)**
339: "And what of Daniel, who received astonishing apocalyptic visions in Babylon?[EN_REF:44]
340: "In his first vision, he beheld the empires of the earth rise and fall—Babylon, Persia, Greece, Rome—and then:
341: *"In my vision at night I looked, and there before me was one like a son of man, coming with the clouds of heaven. He approached the Ancient of Days and was led into his presence. He was given authority, glory and sovereign power; all nations and peoples of every language worshiped him. His dominion is an everlasting dominion that will not pass away, and his kingdom is one that will never be destroyed."* [Dn 7:13-14]
342: "The Son of Man—a heavenly, divine figure who comes upon the clouds of heaven and receives worship and everlasting dominion over every nation! Not a fragile political dynasty, but a Kingdom that shall never be overthrown.
343: "And in the second vision, Daniel was given the exact prophetic timeline for the coming of the Messiah:
344: *"Seventy 'sevens' are decreed for your people and your holy city to finish transgression, to put an end to sin, to atone for wickedness, to bring in everlasting righteousness, to seal up vision and prophecy and to anoint the Most Holy Place."* [Dn 9:24]
345: *"Know and understand this: From the time the word goes out to restore and rebuild Jerusalem until the Anointed One, the ruler, comes, there will be seven 'sevens,' and sixty-two 'sevens.'... After the sixty-two 'sevens,' the Anointed One will be put to death and will have nothing."* [Dn 9:25-26]
346: *'The Anointed One will be cut off'*, he will be put to death! Daniel prophesied that the Messiah would come, make an end of sins, atone for iniquity—and be slain! Do not be confounded, for you know the Scriptures. This was his sacred mission."
347: **32. The Sign of Jonah - Three Days and Three Nights (Jonah 1-2)**
349: Jesus paused. He looked upon the two disciples with gentle compassion, allowing a moment of quiet reflection, and then continued:
350: "Recall the prophet Jonah. When the rulers of Israel demanded a sign from heaven, what were they told? That no sign would be given them except the sign of the prophet Jonah. And what was that sign?
351: "To quiet the raging sea and save the sailors on board, Jonah offered himself as a sacrifice: *'Pick me up and throw me into the sea,' he replied, 'and it will become calm'* [Jon 1:12]. He knew that the death of one would save the many. The tempest of God's wrath subsided when the prophet was swallowed by the deep.
352: *"Now the LORD provided a huge fish to swallow Jonah, and Jonah was in the belly of the fish three days and three nights."* [Jon 1:17]
353: "Friends, in his agony, Jonah prayed that he had cried out from the depths of Sheol—sinking down to the roots of the mountains, the bars of the earth closing over him forever [Jon 2:2, 6].
354: "Jonah was, in figure, dead. Yet on the third day, the Lord commanded the fish, and it vomited Jonah onto dry land [Jon 2:10].
355: "Just as Jonah was three days and three nights in the belly of the great fish, so it was necessary for the Son of Man to be three days and three nights in the heart of the earth! But the tomb could not hold him. The resurrection on the third day announced to you by the women this morning is the supreme sign of God!
356: "And consider what followed: Jonah went and preached to the great city of Nineveh, a heathen nation of pagans, and they repented in dust and ashes. I tell you solemnly: the death and resurrection of the Messiah open wide the gates of salvation, not to the Jews alone, but to every nation upon the earth!"[EN_REF:45]
357: **33. Micah - The Ruler Born in Bethlehem (Micah 5:2)**
359: "Let us not forget Micah, the prophet who pinpointed the very village where the Messiah was to be born:
360: *"But you, Bethlehem Ephrathah, though you are small among the clans of Judah, out of you will come for me one who will be ruler over Israel, whose origins are from of old, from ancient times... He will stand and shepherd his flock in the strength of the LORD, in the majesty of the name of the LORD his God. And they will live securely, for then his greatness will reach to the ends of the earth. And he will be our peace."* [Mic 5:2, 4-5]
361: "Behold! A ruler promised from of old, whose birthplace according to the Scriptures was Bethlehem, the city of David. Yet at the same time, as we have seen, he is the pre-existent, eternal King from everlasting!"[EN_REF:46]
362: **34. Haggai - The Greater Glory of the Second Temple (Haggai 2:6-9)**
364: "Remember how, when the exiles returned and rebuilt the Temple, the elders wept because it seemed so meager compared to Solomon's splendor? Yet the Lord spoke through Haggai:
365: *"This is what the LORD Almighty says: 'In a little while I will once more shake the heavens and the earth, the sea and the dry land. I will shake all nations, and what is desired by all nations will come, and I will fill this house with glory... The glory of this present house will be greater than the glory of the former house.'"* [Hg 2:6-9]
366: "The Desire of all nations promised to visit and fill that house with glory! The glory of the second Temple would surpass that of Solomon—not in gold or silver, but because the Messiah himself would enter its courts and proclaim spiritual riches to you! Believe it!"[EN_REF:47]
367: **35. Zechariah - The Humble King, Thirty Pieces of Silver, and the Pierced One (Zechariah 9-13)**
369: "And Zechariah? Ah, Zechariah saw everything with astonishing, piercing clarity!
371: *"Rejoice greatly, Daughter Zion! Shout, Daughter Jerusalem! See, your king comes to you, righteous and victorious, lowly and riding on a donkey, on a colt, the foal of a donkey."* [Zec 9:9]
372: "You saw this take place only a week ago! He entered Jerusalem riding upon a colt, while the crowds carpeted the road with palm branches, shouting *'Hosanna to the Son of David!'*.
373: "Moreover, when Zechariah served as a shepherd rejected by his own flock, he saw the exact price of betrayal:
374: *"I told them, 'If you think it best, give me my pay; but if not, keep it.' So they paid me thirty pieces of silver. And the LORD said to me, 'Throw it to the potter'—the handsome price at which they valued me! So I took the thirty pieces of silver and threw them to the potter at the house of the LORD."* [Zec 11:12-13]
375: "Thirty pieces of silver! The exact valuation of a common slave! The exact price paid for the betrayal of Jesus Christ by Judas Iscariot![EN_REF:48]
376: "And Zechariah foresaw that most solemn and terrible hour upon the hill of crucifixion:
377: *"And I will pour out on the house of David and the inhabitants of Jerusalem a spirit of grace and supplication. They will look on me, the one they have pierced, and they will mourn for him as one mourns for an only child, and grieve bitterly for him as one grieves for a firstborn son."* [Zec 12:10]
378: *'They will look on me, the one they have pierced!'* It is the Lord who speaks! He declares that he himself would be pierced—and that the people would gaze upon him with bitter mourning! And then God reveals:
379: *"On that day a fountain will be opened to the house of David and the inhabitants of Jerusalem, to cleanse them from sin and impurity."* [Zec 13:1]
380: "From the pierced side of the Savior flows an open fountain of cleansing for all the sin and impurity of Israel!"[EN_REF:49]
381: **36. Malachi - The Messenger of the Covenant and the Sun of Righteousness (Malachi 3:1; 4:5-6)**
383: "And listen now to the final prophetic voice of the Old Testament. Malachi, the seal of the prophets, proclaimed:
384: *"'I will send my messenger, who will prepare the way before me. Then suddenly the Lord you are seeking will come to his temple; the messenger of the covenant, whom you desire, will come,' says the LORD Almighty."* [Mal 3:1]
385: "First would come a messenger—to prepare the way. And immediately following, the Lord himself would enter his temple: the Messenger of the Covenant, the Messiah!
386: "And Malachi closed the revelation of the Old Testament with these timeless words:
387: *"See, I will send the prophet Elijah to you before that great and dreadful day of the LORD comes. He will turn the hearts of the parents to their children, and the hearts of the children to their parents."* [Mal 4:5-6]
388: "You know who that new Elijah was: John, the son of Zechariah, who baptized in the Jordan and pointed to the One coming after him, crying: *'Look, the Lamb of God, who takes away the sin of the world!'*"[EN_REF:50]
